extracted.intended_audience: fiction writers and students of creative writing
extracted.subtask_description: Practical craft guidance for writers of literary fiction, emphasizing place, voice, language, character interiority, and the practice of listening to characters; useful both to produce stories and to evaluate their quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Place
rubrics_metrics.description: Place is not background but generative — a story's setting shapes what can happen and how characters can be.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place anchors emotion and gives stories the texture of reality. Welty calls place foundational ("one of the lesser angels of fiction"). Evaluate whether the setting shapes action and character choices rather than merely decorating the scene.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voice
rubrics_metrics.description: Attention to narrative voice and distinctive speech rhythms; the writer's ear captures character and locale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the prose has a distinctive voice appropriate to the story and characters. Look for rhythmic, regionally inflected, or character-specific speech that feels authentic and consistent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Memory (use of memory in fiction)
rubrics_metrics.description: Memory as a topic/element in craft — how recollection shapes narrative and character.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider how memory is used to structure perspective, reveal interiority, or generate emotional truth; evaluate whether memory is integrated organically rather than imposed as backstory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language / Words Matter
rubrics_metrics.description: The materials of fiction are words; the writer's primary responsibility is to language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge precision, diction, and rhythm. Welty emphasizes precise, rhythmic language — check for economy, sonic quality, and whether word choices produce the intended effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relationship between writers and critics
rubrics_metrics.description: The dynamic and stance a writer takes toward criticism and critics as part of craft discourse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider Welty's caution about theory and criticism: evaluate whether a writer maintains individuality and craft-focused practice rather than writing to please critics or theoretical fashions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relationship between readers and writers
rubrics_metrics.description: How writers conceive their relationship to readers — expectations, trust, and implied contracts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the work trusts readers, rewards attention, and creates the kinds of understandings Welty values (truth, interiority, place), rather than explaining everything or pandering.

rubrics_metrics.name: The mystery of fiction-making
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledgement that why fiction works is partly mysterious and cannot be fully explained; it must be practiced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate humility in craft: recognize imaginative effect that resists full analysis. Avoid forcing mechanical explanations for every narrative 'success.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Fiction is from within / character interiority
rubrics_metrics.description: "In fiction...we write out of ourselves; characters in fiction are conceived from within, and they have their own interior life; they are individuals every time."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether characters feel internally motivated and individualized. Check for believable internal life, distinct desires, and choices that arise naturally from that interiority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Truth through fiction
rubrics_metrics.description: "The novel speaks truth most unmistakably..." — fiction as a means to tell truths that may be inaccessible to nonfiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the work delivers an emotional or experiential truth that would be diminished or impossible in straightforward reportage; consider subtlety, complexity, and moral or psychological insight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Listening as writing
rubrics_metrics.description: The writer's practice of listening — to characters, voices, rhythms — as an essential craft technique.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine whether the author shows evidence of listening: dialogue that rings true, emergent character behavior, and responsiveness to the story's internal sounds rather than imposed exposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Welty's explicit quality checklist (five questions)
rubrics_metrics.description: A concise set of evaluative questions Welty offers for assessing fiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance:
Use these direct questions as an evaluation checklist:
- Does the place feel real, particular, alive?
- Do characters have interior lives?
- Is the language precise and rhythmic?
- Does the work tell a truth that nonfiction couldn't?
- Does the writer listen to their characters?
Apply these to scenes and to the work as a whole when judging effectiveness.
